```{r}
#| include: false
reticulate::use_python(
    Sys.getenv("SCEPTRE_TOUR_PYTHON", path.expand("~/code/research/sceptre-tour-venv/bin/python")),
    required = TRUE

```

This notebook reads the files in `example/` into Python and checks every part
of the format against them. Its twin, `notebook-r.qmd`, does the same in R,
section by section. `SPEC.md` states the rules and `RATIONALE.md` the reasons;
section numbers such as S4 or T3 refer to both. Every output below comes from running the code.

It belongs to the **package suite**: it builds the package's own objects from
the files, on an unreviewed branch build, to test that the files hold
everything an analysis needs. The checks of the format that need no package
are in `verify/`.

`example/` was written by R (`package-suite/make_example.R`) from sceptre's built-in data:

| Dataset | Cells | Responses | gRNAs | Analyses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `highmoi` | 500 | 100 | 60 | `left_sided`, `two_sided`, `singleton`, `bonferroni`, `stopped_after_qc`, `with_resamples` |
| `lowmoi` | 1,000 | 100 | 50 | `default` |
| `types` | 6 | 3 | 2 | none: a synthetic data file with every kind of column |

```{python}
import json, shutil, sys, warnings
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import h5py
import mudata as md
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from scipy import sparse

warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", None)
pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 130)
sys.path.insert(0, "package-suite")
import pysceptre_objects as sf   # the format library, plus building pysceptre objects

screen = Path("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu")
analyses = Path("example/highmoi/analyses")
```

## 1. What is on disk

One file holds the data. Each analysis is a folder.

```{python}
sf.file_listing(analyses / "left_sided")
```

**The data file** is a MuData file. Its modalities are named for what was
measured: `rna` here, and `grna` for the gRNAs (S2). Counts are 32-bit integers,
cells × features, compressed by feature, with 64-bit column pointers (S3, S4).
The file's own metadata is a small native record, which carries the data
file's format version (S10).

```{python}
with h5py.File(screen) as f:
    for modality in f["mod"]:
        group = f[f"mod/{modality}/X"]
        print(f"{modality:9} {group.attrs['encoding-type']}, cells x features = {tuple(int(v) for v in group.attrs['shape'])}; "
              + ", ".join(f"{k}: {group[k].dtype}" for k in ("data", "indices", "indptr")))
    record = f["uns/sceptre"]
    print("uns/sceptre:", {k: record[k].asstr()[()] if record[k].dtype == object else int(record[k][()]) for k in record})
```

**An analysis** starts by naming its data file and which modality of it is
the response (A1). It has a format version of its own:

```{python}
print((analyses / "left_sided/analysis.json").read_text())
```

Each completed stage has a record, written after the stage's tables. It holds
the stage's settings and lists the files the stage wrote (A2):

```{python}
print((analyses / "left_sided/calibration/record.json").read_text())
```

The tables, with their columns:

```{python}
for path in sorted((analyses / "left_sided").rglob("*.parquet")):
    table = pq.read_table(path)
    columns = ", ".join(f"{f.name} ({f.type})" for f in table.schema)
    print(f"{str(path.relative_to(analyses / 'left_sided')):36} {table.num_rows:5} rows: {columns}")
```

## 2. The data file as a MuData

`read_screen()` uses only `mudata`; it needs no sceptre code.

```{python}
mdata = sf.read_screen(screen)
print(mdata)
print(mdata.uns["sceptre"])
```

Cell covariates are split (S5). Facts about the cell are in the shared table:

```{python}
mdata.obs.head(3)
```

Measurements of a modality are in that modality's table, without a prefix:

```{python}
mdata["rna"].obs.head(3)
```

The model's covariate table puts them together, a modality's columns prefixed
with its name:

```{python}
sf.covariate_table(mdata).head(3)
```

pysceptre calls the response modality `response` whatever was measured, so in
an `Analysis` these columns are `response_n_umis` and so on, as they are
today. `read_sceptre_object()` (section 3) does that renaming.

The gRNA table (S8). Its coordinate columns say what they locate: the target.

```{python}
mdata["grna"].var.iloc[[0, 1, 10, 11, 58, 59]]
```

## 3. An analysis as a pysceptre `Analysis`

`read_sceptre_object()` builds pysceptre's own object from the data file and
one analysis folder.

```{python}
analysis = sf.read_sceptre_object(screen, analyses / "left_sided")
analysis
```

```{python}
analysis.get_result("run_discovery_analysis").head(6)
```

## 4. Reading back what the files imply

Several things a package needs are not stored, because they follow from what
is (principle 7). This section rebuilds each one from the files with plain
pandas and compares it with an independent source: pysceptre's own reader,
applied to the same analysis saved by R in the October layout of the `sceptre3`
branch.

```{python}
import pysceptre

saved = sf.read_analysis(analyses / "left_sided")
tables, records = saved["tables"], saved["stages"]
reference = pysceptre.read_analysis("reference-october-layout/highmoi/left_sided")
cells = pd.Index(mdata["rna"].obs_names)
```

**Negative-control groups (T4).** The members of each control group are read
from a table, never taken apart from the group's name.

```{python}
groups = tables["calibration/negative_control_groups"]
members = groups.groupby("grna_group")["grna_id"].apply(list)
members.head(4)
```

```{python}
non_targeting = set(mdata["grna"].var.index[mdata["grna"].var["grna_target"] == "non-targeting"])
tested_groups = set(tables["calibration/results"]["grna_target"])
pd.Series({
    "control groups": len(members),
    "gRNAs per group": sorted(set(members.map(len))),
    "every member is a non-targeting gRNA": set(groups["grna_id"]) <= non_targeting,
    "every group in the calibration results has members": tested_groups == set(members.index),
})
```

**Per-target and per-control cell lists (T1).** The assignment table has one
row per (gRNA, cell). Pooling a target's gRNAs gives the cells a package tests.

```{python}
grna_table = mdata["grna"].var.reset_index(names="grna_id")
grna_table["grna_group"] = sf.grna_groups(grna_table, records["parameters"]["settings"]["grna_integration_strategy"])
by_grna = sf.cells_by_grna(tables["assignment/assignments"], list(mdata["grna"].var_names), cells)
by_target, by_control = sf.group_cells(by_grna, grna_table)

held = reference.assignment
pd.Series({
    "gRNAs": len(by_grna),
    "targets": len(by_target),
    "non-targeting gRNAs": len(by_control),
    "per-gRNA lists equal to pysceptre's": all(np.array_equal(by_grna[k], held.initial[k]) for k in held.initial),
    "per-target unions equal to pysceptre's": all(np.array_equal(by_target[k], held.group_cells[k]) for k in held.group_cells),
    "per-control lists equal to pysceptre's": all(np.array_equal(by_control[k], held.nt_cells[k]) for k in held.nt_cells),
    "gRNAs per cell equal to pysceptre's": np.array_equal(sf.grnas_per_cell(by_grna, len(cells)), held.grnas_per_cell),
})
```

**Which results are significant (T5).** The table does not store the column.
The stage record stores one number, the largest p-value called significant.

```{python}
threshold = records["discovery"]["significance_threshold"]
derived = sf.add_significant(tables["discovery/results"], threshold)
theirs = reference.results["discovery"]
both = derived.merge(theirs, on=["grna_target", "response_id"], suffixes=("", "_reference"))
pd.Series({
    "threshold in the record": threshold,
    "called significant": int(derived["significant"].sum()),
    "equal to the column R computed, for every pair": bool((both["significant"].astype(object) == both["significant_reference"].astype(object)).all()),
})
```

**The log2 fold change (T5).** A results table that has `fold_change` does not
store `log_2_fold_change`; a reader computes it as `log(fold_change) / log(2)`,
which is sceptre's own formula. Under the bonferroni strategy sceptre reports
only the log2 value, so there it is the stored column.

```{python}
def effect_columns(table):
    return ", ".join(c for c in ("fold_change", "se_fold_change", "log_2_fold_change") if c in table)

discovery = tables["discovery/results"]
both = sf.add_log_2_fold_change(discovery).merge(theirs, on=["grna_target", "response_id"], suffixes=("", "_reference"))
bonferroni = sf.read_analysis(analyses / "bonferroni")["tables"]["discovery/results"]
pd.Series({
    "effect columns stored (union strategy)": effect_columns(discovery),
    "derived log2 identical to R's column, for every pair": np.array_equal(
        both["log_2_fold_change"].to_numpy(float), both["log_2_fold_change_reference"].to_numpy(float), equal_nan=True),
    "effect columns stored (bonferroni strategy)": effect_columns(bonferroni),
})
```

**The design matrix (T7).** The record stores the formula and a hash. Python
rebuilds the matrix from the formula and the covariates in the data file.

```{python}
settings = records["parameters"]["settings"]
design = sf.design_matrix(settings["formula"], sf.covariate_table(mdata))
pd.Series({
    "formula": settings["formula"],
    "terms rebuilt": ", ".join(design.terms),
    "terms equal to the record's": design.terms == records["parameters"]["design"]["terms"],
    "hash in the record (written by R)": records["parameters"]["design"]["sha256"][:16] + "...",
    "hash of the matrix rebuilt here": sf.design_sha256(design.matrix)[:16] + "...",
    "equal": sf.design_sha256(design.matrix) == records["parameters"]["design"]["sha256"],
})
```

Only additive formulas of covariate names, `log(x)` and `log(x + 1)` can be
written:

```{python}
for formula in (settings["formula"], "~log(rna_n_umis) * batch", "~poly(rna_n_umis, 2)"):
    print(sf.formula_in_subset(formula), formula)
```

**Resampled statistics (T5).** `with_resamples` kept every resampled statistic.
In the file they are one list per pair; pysceptre gets them back as the columns
it expects.

```{python}
resamples = sf.read_analysis(analyses / "with_resamples")["tables"]["discovery/resamples"]
wide = sf.read_sceptre_object(screen, analyses / "with_resamples").results["discovery"]
pd.Series({
    "pairs": len(resamples),
    "statistics per pair": f"{resamples['z_null'].map(len).min()} to {resamples['z_null'].map(len).max()}",
    "columns in the file's table": ", ".join(resamples.columns),
    "z_null_ columns in the object's table": len(sf.resample_columns(wide)),
})
```

## 5. Several analyses, two datasets

Each dataset is read from one file; only the analysis differs.

```{python}
rows = []
for dataset in ("highmoi", "lowmoi"):
    for folder in sorted(Path(f"example/{dataset}/analyses").iterdir()):
        saved_analysis = sf.read_analysis(folder)
        s = saved_analysis["stages"]
        discovery = saved_analysis["tables"].get("discovery/results")
        cut = s["discovery"]["significance_threshold"] if "discovery" in s else None
        rows.append({
            "dataset": dataset,
            "analysis": folder.name,
            "stages run": ", ".join(s),
            "side": s["parameters"]["settings"]["side"],
            "strategy": s["parameters"]["settings"]["grna_integration_strategy"],
            "control group": s["parameters"]["settings"]["control_group"],
            "assignment": s["assignment"]["settings"]["method"],
            "cells in use": int(saved_analysis["tables"]["qc/cells"]["in_use"].sum()),
            "discoveries": "" if discovery is None else int(sf.add_significant(discovery, cut)["significant"].sum()),
        })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

(`continued_in_python` appears here once section 8 has run.)

## 6. Round trip in Python

Every analysis is read into pysceptre and written to a new folder. The two
sets of files are then compared.

```{python}
copy = Path("roundtrip/python-copy")
shutil.rmtree(copy, ignore_errors=True)
r_written = {
    dataset: sorted(p.name for p in Path(f"example/{dataset}/analyses").iterdir() if p.name != "continued_in_python")
    for dataset in ("highmoi", "lowmoi")
}

def column_types(folder, table):
    path = Path(folder) / f"{table}.parquet"
    if table == sf.FITS:   # the fit cache is a folder of part files
        path = sorted((Path(folder) / table).glob("*.parquet"))[0]
    return [(f.name, str(f.type)) for f in pq.read_schema(path)]

rows = []
for dataset, names in r_written.items():
    source = Path(f"example/{dataset}")
    sf.write_sceptre_screen(sf.read_sceptre_object(source / "screen.h5mu"), copy / dataset / "screen.h5mu")
    for name in names:
        loaded = sf.read_sceptre_object(source / "screen.h5mu", source / "analyses" / name)
        written = sf.write_sceptre_analysis(loaded, copy / dataset / "screen.h5mu", copy / dataset / "analyses" / name)
        a, b = sf.read_analysis(source / "analyses" / name), sf.read_analysis(written)
        rows.append({
            "dataset": dataset,
            "analysis": name,
            "link equal": a["screen"] == b["screen"] and a["response_modality"] == b["response_modality"],
            "stage records equal": a["stages"] == b["stages"],
            "tables": len(a["tables"]),
            "tables equal": sum(sf.same_table(a["tables"][k], b["tables"][k]) for k in a["tables"]),
            "same column names and types": sum(
                column_types(source / "analyses" / name, k) == column_types(written, k)
                for k in a["tables"]),
        })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

The data file written by Python has the same number types as the one written
by R, and the same contents:

```{python}
def count_types(path):
    with h5py.File(path) as f:
        return {m: {k: str(f[f"mod/{m}/X/{k}"].dtype) for k in ("data", "indices", "indptr")} for m in f["mod"]}

rows = []
for dataset in r_written:
    x, y = sf.read_screen(f"example/{dataset}/screen.h5mu"), sf.read_screen(copy / dataset / "screen.h5mu")
    rows.append({
        "dataset": dataset,
        "count types equal": count_types(f"example/{dataset}/screen.h5mu") == count_types(copy / dataset / "screen.h5mu"),
        "counts equal": all((x[m].X != y[m].X).nnz == 0 for m in ("rna", "grna")),
        "cell tables equal": x.obs.equals(y.obs) and all(x[m].obs.equals(y[m].obs) for m in ("rna", "grna")),
        "feature tables equal": all(x[m].var.equals(y[m].var) for m in ("rna", "grna")),
        "metadata equal": x.uns["sceptre"] == y.uns["sceptre"],
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

The Parquet files are not byte-identical: R's writer marks a column without
missing values as required and Python's marks every column optional. Names,
types and values are the same.

## 7. Across languages

The files read above were written by R. As an independent check, each object
built from them is compared with what pysceptre's own reader gives for the same
analysis saved by R in the October layout.

```{python}
rows = []
for dataset, names in r_written.items():
    source = Path(f"example/{dataset}")
    for name in [None] + names:
        ours = sf.read_sceptre_object(source / "screen.h5mu", name and source / "analyses" / name)
        theirs = pysceptre.read_analysis(f"reference-october-layout/{dataset}/{name or 'imported'}")
        rows.append({"dataset": dataset, "analysis": name or "(data only)", "comparison": sf.comparison_summary(sf.compare_analyses(ours, theirs))})
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

## 8. Continue in Python an analysis that R stopped

This section is about parity between the two packages, not about the format:
the format's part is only to carry what each needs to continue.

`stopped_after_qc` was run in R through QC. Python reads it, runs the three
testing stages, and saves the result as a new analysis of the same data file.

```{python}
continued = sf.read_sceptre_object(screen, analyses / "stopped_after_qc")
print("as read:  ", continued)
continued = continued.run_calibration_check().run_power_check().run_discovery_analysis()
print("continued:", continued)

shutil.rmtree(analyses / "continued_in_python", ignore_errors=True)
written = sf.write_sceptre_analysis(continued, screen, analyses / "continued_in_python")
```

Each stage record says which package ran the stage:

```{python}
saved_continued = sf.read_analysis(analyses / "continued_in_python")
pd.DataFrame({s: r["provenance"] for s, r in saved_continued["stages"].items()}).T
```

R ran the same settings to the end as `left_sided`. The two sets of discovery
p-values:

```{python}
mine = saved_continued["tables"]["discovery/results"]
theirs = sf.read_analysis(analyses / "left_sided")["tables"]["discovery/results"]
both = mine.merge(theirs, on=["grna_target", "response_id"], suffixes=("_python", "_r"))
tested = (both["pass_qc_python"] & both["pass_qc_r"]).to_numpy(dtype=bool)
pd.Series({
    "pairs": len(both),
    "pairs tested in both": int(tested.sum()),
    "largest relative difference in p-value": f"{np.max(np.abs(both.loc[tested, 'p_value_python'] / both.loc[tested, 'p_value_r'] - 1)):.1e}",
    "discoveries, Python": int(sf.add_significant(mine, saved_continued["stages"]["discovery"]["significance_threshold"])["significant"].sum()),
    "discoveries, R": int(sf.add_significant(theirs, records["discovery"]["significance_threshold"])["significant"].sum()),
})
```

## 9. What a reader tolerates and what it refuses

```{python}
variants = Path("roundtrip/variants-python")
shutil.rmtree(variants, ignore_errors=True)

def variant(name):
    """A fresh copy of the left_sided analysis to modify."""
    shutil.copytree(analyses / "left_sided", variants / name)
    return variants / name

def attempt(read):
    try:
        read()
        print("Read without complaint.")
    except Exception as error:
        print("Refused:", error)

original = sf.read_sceptre_object(screen, analyses / "left_sided")
```

**A table in pieces, with an unknown column and dictionary-encoded identifiers
(T0).** The assignment table is replaced by a folder of three part files.

```{python}
folder = variant("parts")
table = pq.read_table(folder / "assignment/assignments.parquet")
(folder / "assignment/assignments.parquet").unlink()
(folder / "assignment/assignments.parquet").mkdir()
size = -(-table.num_rows // 3)
for i in range(3):
    part = table.slice(i * size, size)
    part = pa.table({
        "grna_id": part["grna_id"].dictionary_encode(),
        "cell_id": part["cell_id"].dictionary_encode(),
        "score": np.linspace(0, 1, part.num_rows),   # a column this reader does not know
    })
    pq.write_table(part, folder / "assignment/assignments.parquet" / f"part-{i:05d}.parquet")
print(sorted(p.name for p in (folder / "assignment/assignments.parquet").iterdir()))
print(sf.comparison_summary(sf.compare_analyses(sf.read_sceptre_object(screen, folder), original)))
```

**Another data file (A1).** An analysis refuses a data file that was subset,
even if it kept the dataset's identifier, and a data file that was imported
again.

```{python}
subset = mdata[:400].copy()
subset.uns["sceptre"] = dict(mdata.uns["sceptre"])
sf.write_screen(subset, variants / "subset.h5mu")
attempt(lambda: sf.read_sceptre_object(variants / "subset.h5mu", analyses / "left_sided"))

again = sf.read_screen(screen)
again.uns["sceptre"] = {"moi": "high"}             # no identifier: the writer assigns a new one
sf.write_screen(again, variants / "imported_again.h5mu")
attempt(lambda: sf.read_sceptre_object(variants / "imported_again.h5mu", analyses / "left_sided"))
```

**Modality names, and modalities an analysis does not use (S2, A1).** The same
data is written under the modality name `atac`, with a hashing modality beside
it. With two candidates, a reader must be told which is the response; an
analysis folder says so itself.

```{python}
renamed = sf.analysis_screen(sf.read_sceptre_object(screen), response_modality="atac")
hto = sparse.csc_matrix((np.full(renamed.n_obs, 5), (np.arange(renamed.n_obs), np.arange(renamed.n_obs) % 2)), shape=(renamed.n_obs, 2))
other = md.MuData({
    "atac": renamed["atac"], "grna": renamed["grna"],
    "hashing": ad.AnnData(X=hto, obs=pd.DataFrame(index=renamed["grna"].obs_names), var=pd.DataFrame(index=["hto_1", "hto_2"])),
})
for name in renamed.obs.columns:
    other.obs[name] = renamed.obs[name].array
other.uns["sceptre"] = dict(renamed.uns["sceptre"])
sf.write_screen(other, variants / "atac_with_hashing.h5mu")
print(list(count_types(variants / "atac_with_hashing.h5mu")))
attempt(lambda: sf.read_screen(variants / "atac_with_hashing.h5mu"))
```

```{python}
def check_other(file, folder):
    back = sf.read_sceptre_object(file, folder)
    return pd.Series({
        "response modality named by the analysis": sf.analysis_response_modality(folder),
        "formula in the parameters record": json.loads((Path(folder) / "parameters/record.json").read_text())["settings"]["formula"],
        "object compared with the original": sf.comparison_summary(sf.compare_analyses(back, original)),
    })

written = sf.write_sceptre_analysis(original, variants / "atac_with_hashing.h5mu", variants / "atac_analysis", response_modality="atac")
check_other(variants / "atac_with_hashing.h5mu", variants / "atac_analysis")
```

**A table that is not what its stage wrote (A5).** Each stage record lists its
files and their row counts.

```{python}
folder = variant("truncated")
cells_table = pq.read_table(folder / "qc/cells.parquet")
pq.write_table(cells_table.slice(0, 450), folder / "qc/cells.parquet")
attempt(lambda: sf.read_analysis(folder))
```

**Rerunning a stage (A4).** Clearing a stage removes its record and files and
those of every later stage, so the folder never holds stale results.

```{python}
folder = variant("rerun")
print("before:", sf.stages_run(folder), "-", sum(1 for p in folder.rglob("*") if p.is_file()), "files")
sf.clear_stage(folder, "qc")
print("after: ", sf.stages_run(folder), "-", sum(1 for p in folder.rglob("*") if p.is_file()), "files")
print(sf.read_sceptre_object(screen, folder))
```

**The fit cache (T6).** Fitted response models are kept in `fits/response/`,
outside the stage folders: no stage owns them, and any testing stage can use
or add to them. Clearing a testing stage leaves them; clearing QC removes them.

```{python}
folder = variant("fits_kept")
sf.clear_stage(folder, "calibration")
print("after clearing calibration:", sf.stages_run(folder), "- fits kept:", (folder / "fits/response/identity.json").exists())
sf.clear_stage(folder, "qc")
print("after clearing qc:         ", sf.stages_run(folder), "- fits kept:", (folder / "fits/response/identity.json").exists())
```

A cached fit is reused only if it was made as this analysis would make it.
Here the record of how the fits were made is changed to another fitting
method.

```{python}
print("fits reused as written:", len(original.response_fits()))
folder = variant("other_fit_method")
identity = json.loads((folder / "fits/response/identity.json").read_text())
identity["response_fit_method"] = "sceptre"
n = (folder / "fits/response/identity.json").write_text(json.dumps(identity, indent=2))
changed = sf.read_sceptre_object(screen, folder)
print("fits reused after the change:", len(changed.response_fits()))
```

**Every kind of column (S7).** `example/types/screen.h5mu` is a small synthetic
data file written by R with a factor whose levels are not alphabetical, a text
covariate, a true/false covariate, a covariate with missing values, and a gRNA
table with missing text and a missing integer. Python reads it:

```{python}
def describe(frame):
    def kind(column):
        if isinstance(column.dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype):
            return "categorical: " + ", ".join(map(str, column.cat.categories))
        if pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(column.dtype):
            return "integer"
        if pd.api.types.is_float_dtype(column.dtype):
            return "double"
        return "text"
    def text(value):
        if pd.isna(value):
            return "NA"
        return f"{value:g}" if isinstance(value, (float, np.floating)) else str(value)
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "kind": {name: kind(frame[name]) for name in frame.columns},
        "values": {name: ", ".join(text(v) for v in frame[name]) for name in frame.columns},
    })

from_r = sf.read_screen("example/types/screen.h5mu")
pd.concat([describe(sf.covariate_table(from_r)), describe(from_r["grna"].var)])
```

Python then builds the same data itself, writes it, and reads that back:

```{python}
ids = [f"cell_{i}" for i in range(1, 7)]
counts = sparse.csc_matrix(np.array([[3, 0, 5, 0, 0, 2], [1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0], [0, 2, 0, 0, 4, 0]]).T)
grna_counts = sparse.csc_matrix(np.array([[7, 0, 4, 0, 8, 0], [0, 9, 0, 6, 0, 5]]).T)
built = md.MuData({
    "rna": ad.AnnData(X=counts, obs=pd.DataFrame({
        "n_umis": np.asarray(counts.sum(axis=1)).reshape(-1).astype(float),
        "n_nonzero": np.asarray((counts > 0).sum(axis=1)).reshape(-1).astype(np.int32),
    }, index=ids), var=pd.DataFrame(index=["gene_1", "gene_2", "gene_3"])),
    "grna": ad.AnnData(X=grna_counts, obs=pd.DataFrame({
        "n_umis": np.asarray(grna_counts.sum(axis=1)).reshape(-1).astype(float),
        "n_nonzero": np.asarray((grna_counts > 0).sum(axis=1)).reshape(-1).astype(np.int32),
    }, index=ids), var=pd.DataFrame({
        "grna_target": ["site_1", "non-targeting"], "target_chr": ["chr1", None], "target_start": pd.array([100, None], dtype="Int32"),
        "target_end": pd.array([149, None], dtype="Int32"),
    }, index=["grna_a", "grna_nt"])),
})
built.obs["batch"] = pd.Categorical(["b", "a", "b", "a", "b", "a"], categories=["b", "a"])
built.obs["lane"] = ["L2", "L1", "L2", "L1", "L2", "L1"]
built.obs["treated"] = [True, False, True, True, False, False]
built.obs["score"] = [0.5, np.nan, 1.5, 2.5, np.nan, 3.5]
built.obs["S.Score"] = [0.5, -1.25, 1.5, 2.5, 0.125, 3.5]
built.uns["sceptre"] = {
    "moi": "low", "name": "Synthetic file with every kind of column", "source": "https://example.org/no-such-dataset",
    "perturbation_type": "CRISPRi", "organism": "Homo sapiens", "genome_build": "GRCh38",
}
sf.write_screen(built, copy / "types" / "screen.h5mu")

from_python = sf.read_screen(copy / "types" / "screen.h5mu")
pd.Series({
    "covariates equal to the R-written file's": describe(sf.covariate_table(from_python)).equals(describe(sf.covariate_table(from_r))),
    "gRNA table equal": describe(from_python["grna"].var).equals(describe(from_r["grna"].var)),
    "counts equal": all((from_python[m].X != from_r[m].X).nnz == 0 for m in ("rna", "grna")),
    "count types equal": count_types(copy / "types" / "screen.h5mu") == count_types("example/types/screen.h5mu"),
})
```

**A covariate with a dot in its name (S5.4, T7.1).** The types file has the
covariate `S.Score`. R takes such a name in a formula as it is. pysceptre's
formula parser does not, so the prototype gives the column a dot-free alias
for the call. The R notebook builds the same matrix and compares the hash
written here.

```{python}
dotted = sf.design_matrix("~log(rna_n_umis) + S.Score + batch", sf.covariate_table(from_r))
n = Path("roundtrip/dotted-design.json").write_text(json.dumps({"terms": dotted.terms, "sha256": sf.design_sha256(dotted.matrix)}))
pd.Series({"terms": ", ".join(dotted.terms), "hash": sf.design_sha256(dotted.matrix)[:16] + "..."})
```

## 10. Checking files against the specification

`validate_screen()` and `validate_analysis()` check files against the numbered
rules of `SPEC.md`. They read the files directly, build no pysceptre object,
and report every problem they find. The R library has the same two functions.
What they check about a data file's structure comes from `spec/screen.json`,
about tables from `spec/tables.json`, and about the JSON records from two JSON
Schemas. The example conforms:

```{python}
print(len(sf.validate_screen(screen)), len(sf.validate_analysis(analyses / "left_sided", screen)))
```

`conformance/` holds files that conform and files that each break one rule
(`make_conformance.py` builds them). Three of the broken ones, with what the
validator reports. The first is *readable*: it does not conform, and a reader
must still accept it (S4.4).

```{python}
cases = {case["name"]: case for case in json.loads(Path("conformance/cases.json").read_text())}

def check(case):
    if case["kind"] == "screen":
        return sf.validate_screen(case["path"])
    return sf.validate_analysis(case["path"], case.get("screen"))

for name in ("invalid/screens/counts_as_uint16.h5mu", "invalid/analyses/stage_without_its_predecessor", "invalid/analyses/side_up"):
    print(f"{name}: {cases[name]['what']}")
    found = check(cases[name])
    print(found.to_string(index=False))
    print("->", sf.conformance_level(found), end="\n\n")
```

Every case, with the rules expected and the rules reported:

```{python}
found = {name: check(case) for name, case in cases.items()}
reported = {name: sorted(set(problems["rule"])) for name, problems in found.items()}
level = {name: sf.conformance_level(problems) for name, problems in found.items()}
as_expected = {name: reported[name] == case["expect"] and level[name] == case["level"] for name, case in cases.items()}
pd.DataFrame({
    "expected": {name: ", ".join(case["expect"]) for name, case in cases.items()},
    "reported": {name: ", ".join(rules) for name, rules in reported.items()},
    "level": level,
    "as expected": as_expected,
})
```

The four readable files are then read, and give the same counts as the
conforming file each was made from:

```{python}
def same_counts(a, b):
    x, y = sf.read_screen(a), sf.read_screen(b)
    return all((x[m].X != y[m].X).nnz == 0 for m in y.mod)

pd.Series({name: same_counts(case["path"], case["reads_as"]) for name, case in cases.items() if case["level"] == "readable"})
```

```{python}
r_results = json.loads(Path("conformance/results-r.json").read_text())
by_level = lambda which: f"{sum(as_expected[n] for n in cases if cases[n]['level'] == which)} of {sum(1 for n in cases if cases[n]['level'] == which)}"
pd.Series({
    "cases": len(cases),
    "conforming files, accepted": by_level("conforming"),
    "readable files, reported as readable with the expected rules": by_level("readable"),
    "unreadable files, reported with exactly the expected rules": by_level("not readable"),
    "rules exercised by a broken file": len({rule for case in cases.values() for rule in case["expect"]}),
    "the R validator reports the same rules and levels for every case": all(
        reported[n] == sorted(r_results[n]["rules"]) and level[n] == r_results[n]["level"] for n in cases),
})
```
